name: Ghana
description: Ghana is a politically stable, English-speaking West African nation offering a warm welcome to expats, particularly those of African descent seeking to reconnect with their heritage. Its growing economy, rich culture, and strategic location make it an appealing destination for professionals, entrepreneurs, and retirees looking for a vibrant African experience.
longdescription: Expat life in Ghana, especially in the capital Accra, is characterized by a blend of vibrant culture and modern conveniences, though certain infrastructure challenges persist. The country boasts a stable democratic governance and a population renowned for its hospitality. English is the official language, facilitating communication for many expats. The economy, driven by sectors like oil and gas, telecommunications, mining, and agriculture, is growing, offering opportunities for qualified professionals and investors. Accra's quality of life is on an improving trajectory, with expanding consumer services, private clinics, and modern residential developments. However, expats often face high costs for housing and imported goods, referred to as the 'expat premium,' and traffic congestion in Accra can be a significant daily challenge. While generally safe, petty crime is prevalent in crowded areas, and power cuts (locally known as 'dumsor') remain a reality, necessitating properties with backup power. Healthcare infrastructure is improving, particularly in major cities with private facilities, but comprehensive international health insurance is highly recommended.

visas.name: Ghana Work Permit
visas.description: Employment permit for foreign nationals working with Ghanaian companies. Ghana is West Africa's most stable and business-friendly destination for expats.
benefits: Legal right to work
English-speaking environment
Gateway to West Africa
Growing tech ecosystem
Rich cultural heritage
required_documents: Passport
Employment contract
Educational certificates
Medical certificate
Police clearance

visas.name: Ghana Investor Visa
visas.description: Residence permit for foreign investors registering a business with the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC). Minimum investment thresholds apply.
benefits: Business ownership rights
Access to West African markets
English-speaking country
Renewable residence
Stable democracy
visas.path_to_residency_description: Investors may apply for permanent residence after sustained business operations.
required_documents: Passport
GIPC registration certificate
Business registration
Proof of investment
Bank statements

visas.name: Student Permit / Study Entry and Residence Permit
visas.description: The Student Permit / Study Entry and Residence Permit in Ghana is for foreign nationals who have gained admission to a recognized educational institution in Ghana and wish to reside in the country for the duration of their studies. It allows the holder to legally stay in Ghana for educational purposes.
visas.target_applicant: International students who have received an official acceptance letter from an accredited Ghanaian university or college.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable annually, provided the student maintains enrollment in a recognized educational institution and continues to meet the eligibility criteria. Renewal requires an application letter from the school, original renewed Non-Citizen ID card, recent passport pictures, and proof of payment of school fees.
benefits: Legal right to reside in Ghana for the purpose of study.
Opportunity to work part-time during academic terms and full-time during breaks.
Cultural immersion and experience of living in Ghana.
Access to Ghanaian educational institutions.
required_documents: Application letter from the school addressed to the Comptroller-General of the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS)
Two (2) recent passport-sized photographs
Copies of admission letter from an accredited Ghanaian institution
Copies of school fees receipts or proof of payment of fees
Valid passport with at least six months validity beyond planned stay, to be submitted with the application
Copy of Non-Citizen Identification Card (mandatory for foreign nationals staying over 90 days)
Proof of sufficient financial means to cover tuition and living expenses (e.g., bank statements, scholarship letter)
Medical certificate from an accredited health institution, confirming freedom from contagious diseases
Valid health insurance policy
Police Clearance Certificate (where required for general residence permits)
Completed residence permit application form (obtained from GIS)
Introductory letter from the International Programmes Office (IPO) of the educational institution (where applicable)
Bond to be executed (where applicable)
Copies of Birth Certificate (where applicable)
Sworn affidavit (where applicable)
Letter of support from Guarantor (where applicable)
application_process_steps: Obtain an official acceptance letter from a recognized Ghanaian educational institution.
Apply for a student entry visa at the nearest Ghanaian embassy or consulate in your home country (if not from an ECOWAS country or visa-exempt).
Upon arrival in Ghana, apply for a Non-Citizen Ghana Card, which is a mandatory prerequisite for the residence permit.
Gather all required documents, including the application letter from the school, admission letter, passport, photographs, proof of funds, medical certificate, and fees.
Submit the complete application package for the Student Residence Permit to the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS).
Attend any required interviews or biometric appointments.

visas.name: Investor Permit / Business Investment Visa
visas.description: The Ghana Investor Permit, often referred to as a Business Investment Visa, allows foreign nationals to reside in Ghana based on their investment in a Ghanaian enterprise. It provides the legal foundation for the investor to manage their investment and is closely linked to registration with the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC).
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign shareholders, founders, directors, and business owners establishing or investing capital into a compliant company in Ghana.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Investor Permit provides a legal foundation for long-term residence. Investors who maintain their investment and comply with regulations may renew their permits, potentially leading to an Indefinite Residence Permit over time.
visas.renewal_conditions: The business must continue to comply with GIPC regulations, immigration laws, tax obligations, and sector-specific requirements where applicable.
visas.tax_implications: GIPC-registered companies may be eligible for investment guarantees, repatriation rights, and tax incentives such as tax holidays and customs duty exemptions in specific sectors. The standard corporate tax rate in Ghana is 25%.
benefits: Legal right to reside in Ghana based on investment.
Ability to legally manage and oversee one's enterprise in Ghana.
Potential qualification for Immigrant Quotas, authorizing employment of foreign nationals within the enterprise.
Access to investment guarantees and repatriation rights.
Eligibility for tax incentives and exemptions in specific sectors.
required_documents: Completed Investor Permit application form issued by GIS
Valid passport with sufficient validity to cover the intended stay
Recent passport-sized photographs
GIS medical examination report
Non-Citizen ID Card issued by the National Identification Authority
Company registration certificates (Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Commencement, Company's Constitution)
GIPC registration evidence (including verification of capital injection)
Proof of capital investment (bank evidence, audited accounts, or capital confirmation documents)
Tax compliance documents (e.g., Tax Identification Number)
Police Clearance Certificate from home country
application_process_steps: Register the business with the Registrar-General's Department (obtain Certificate of Incorporation, etc.).
Register the enterprise with the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC) and demonstrate compliance with minimum capital thresholds.
Undergo a mandatory medical examination conducted or approved by the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS).
Obtain a Non-Citizen ID Card from the National Identification Authority for stays exceeding 90 days.
Compile all required supporting documentation, including company and GIPC registration, proof of capital, passport, photographs, and tax documents.
Submit the Investor Permit application to the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) in Accra.

visas.name: Dependant Residence Permit (Family Reunification)
visas.description: The Dependant Residence Permit in Ghana allows eligible family members of foreign nationals living and working in Ghana, or Ghanaian nationals who have acquired foreign passports, to legally reside in the country. This permit is for legally married spouses and minor children and does not automatically confer the right to work in Ghana.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a legally married spouse or a minor child of a foreign national holding a valid Residence Permit in Ghana, or a Ghanaian national with a foreign passport, who intends to reside with the main applicant in Ghana.
visas.path_to_residency_description: While the Dependant Residence Permit itself is not a direct path to permanent residency, the main applicant (or the dependant individually, if they meet separate criteria) may be eligible for an 'Indefinite Residence Permit' after meeting specific residency durations and other requirements (e.g., 5-6 years of continuous residence or 3 years if married to a Ghanaian citizen). This would then allow the holder to reside permanently in Ghana.
visas.renewal_conditions: The principal applicant must maintain a valid immigration status, and the family must continue to meet the eligibility requirements. The dependant must reside with the main applicant in Ghana. Any previous permit terms must not have been violated.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of a Dependant Residence Permit, if considered tax residents (typically by spending 183 days or more in Ghana within a 12-month period), will be taxed on their worldwide income. There are no special tax exemptions or treatments specifically for this permit category; standard Ghanaian income tax rules apply.
benefits: Legal right to reside in Ghana for the duration of the main applicant's permit.
Ability to travel in and out of Ghana multiple times within the permit's validity without a separate visa.
Opportunity to remain with family in Ghana, fostering family reunification.
required_documents: Completed Dependant Residence Permit application form issued by GIS
Application letter requesting for residence permit
Valid passport with sufficient validity to cover the intended stay
Recent passport-sized photographs (2)
Non-Citizen ID Card (required for all dependants staying more than 90 days)
GIS medical examination report
Proof of Family Relationship (Marriage certificate for spouses; Birth certificates for children showing parentage)
Authenticated and translated foreign-issued certificates (where applicable)
Copy of the main applicant's valid Residence Permit or Residence Permit receipt
Letter of support from the main applicant confirming financial responsibility for the dependant
Copy of the main applicant's passport bio-data page
Copy of the main applicant's Work Permit approval (if applicable, for employment-based residence)
Copy of bank statement/indenture (from the main applicant or guarantor, as evidence of support)
Letter of consent from child's parents (where applicable)
Statutory declaration (affidavit) by guardian from the high court (where applicable)
Two guarantors with copies of their Ghanaian passport/national identification card (if required by GIS)
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility as a recognized dependant under Ghanaian immigration law (legally married spouse or minor child).
Verify the main applicant's valid immigration status (e.g., existing Residence Permit or Work Permit).
Complete the mandatory GIS medical examination.
Obtain the Non-Citizen ID Card (mandatory for all foreign nationals staying more than 90 days).
Gather all required supporting documentation, ensuring foreign documents are authenticated and translated.
Submit the completed Dependant Residence Permit application directly to the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) in Accra.
Respond promptly to any requests for additional documents or clarifications from GIS.
Collect the approved Dependant Residence Permit once processing is complete.

visas.name: Retiree Residence Permit (informal name for a type of Dependant Residence Permit)
visas.description: This permit is for foreign nationals who are no longer in active employment and wish to reside in Ghana. Although informally known as a 'Retiree Residence Permit', it is officially issued as a Dependant Residence Permit by the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS). It allows the holder to live in Ghana for an extended period, typically without engaging in employment for financial reward.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign nationals aged 60 or above who have retired from active employment and possess sufficient financial means to support themselves in Ghana without seeking employment.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After accumulating at least 6 years of legal residence within the 8 years prior to applying (with 12 continuous months immediately preceding the application), retirees may be eligible to apply for an Indefinite Residence Permit, provided they also demonstrate a substantial contribution to Ghana's development.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be renewed for a further 4 years, for a maximum total of 8 years. Renewal requires maintaining eligibility criteria, including financial self-sufficiency and adherence to permit conditions. The renewal process is treated as a new application.
benefits: Legal residency in Ghana for up to 4 years initially, renewable for a total of 8 years.
Opportunity to reside in a stable democracy with English as the official language.
Potential pathway to Indefinite Residence Permit after meeting long-term residency requirements.
Access to local services and banking.
Freedom of movement in and out of Ghana within the permit's validity period.
required_documents: Application letter requesting the residence permit, addressed to the Comptroller-General, stating personal details, reasons, and duration.
Form F (completed and signed application form).
Two recent passport-sized photographs.
Valid passport (original).
Proof of retirement (e.g., pension documents).
Proof of financial sufficiency (bank statements, proof of pension income, or lease agreement demonstrating sufficient funds to maintain self and any dependents without public funds).
Medical examination report from GIS Clinic.
Police Clearance Certificate from country of residence.
Valid Non-Citizen ID card from the NIA.
Two Ghanaian guarantors with copies of their national IDs (or Ghanaian passports).
A personal letter of guarantee from one of the two Ghanaian guarantors.
Executed security bond (Form I) by both guarantors, making them liable for deportation costs.
Marriage Certificate (if applicable, for spouse's separate application).
Birth Certificate of child (if applicable, for child's separate application).
Proof of immovable property (indenture, site plan etc., where applicable).
application_process_steps: Obtain and complete Form F from the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS).
Prepare an application letter addressed to the Comptroller-General of GIS, stating personal details, reasons for the permit, and requested duration.
Gather all required supporting documents, including passport, photographs, financial proofs, medical report, police clearance, and guarantor documents.
Submit the completed application form and all supporting documents to the Ghana Immigration Service.
Pay the applicable government fees for the permit, medical tests, and Non-Citizen ID card.
Attend any required interviews or provide additional information if requested by GIS.

visas.name: Indefinite Residence Permit (Permanent Residency)
visas.description: The Indefinite Residence Permit in Ghana allows foreign nationals to reside permanently in the country. It is granted to individuals who have established strong ties to Ghana, demonstrated good character, and contributed meaningfully to the country's development, without the need for periodic permit renewals.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign nationals who have lawfully resided in Ghana for a significant period (typically five years within seven, or two years for foreign spouses of Ghanaian citizens) and can demonstrate a substantial contribution to the country's development.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This is the permanent residency status itself. It allows indefinite stay in Ghana, but is not Ghanaian citizenship, which is a separate application process.
benefits: Entitlement to remain indefinitely in Ghana.
Entitlement to enter Ghana without a visa.
Entitlement to work in Ghana as a self-employed individual or employee without a work permit.
Eligibility to apply for dependant permits for non-Ghanaian children or other non-Ghanaian dependants.
required_documents: Completed application form
Two (2) current passport size photographs
Application letter from applicant/sponsor
Attestation letter by two (2) Ghanaians (Notaries Public, Lawyers with Practicing Certificate, or Senior Public Officers) with copies of their national ID
Photocopy of applicant's passport (bio-data and current residence permit pages)
Evidence of immovable properties (indenture, site plan, etc., where applicable)

Company's Documents (Companies Code, audited account for past three years, SSNIT returns of Ghanaian employees, G.I.P.C Certificate, Tax Clearance Certificate for past six years - if applicable, showing business ownership/contribution)
Evidence of social contributions (e.g., donations, charity work, where applicable)
Current police report from Ghana
Curriculum Vitae of applicant
Medical report from an examination conducted at the Ghana Immigration Service Clinic
Non-Citizen ID Card
Valid residence permit with at least six months' validity at the time of application
Proof of financial stability and means of support
Evidence of contribution to Ghana's development (e.g., business ownership, community involvement, investments, professional service)
For foreign spouses: Support letter from Ghanaian spouse, spouse's birth certificate, and marriage certificate
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility criteria, including required residency period and contribution to Ghana.
Assemble all required documents, including completed application form, passport photos, police report, medical report, and financial proofs.
Submit the application and supporting documents to the Ghana Immigration Service (Headquarters).
The Ghana Immigration Service will conduct due diligence and background checks.
A report is submitted to the Minister for the Interior for final approval.
Upon approval, the Indefinite Residence Permit is issued.

visas.name: Right of Abode
visas.description: The Right of Abode (ROA) is a permanent legal status in Ghana, granted with presidential approval, allowing eligible individuals to live and work in the country indefinitely. It is considered the highest level of residency status short of full citizenship and is primarily designed for former Ghanaians who lost their citizenship and persons of African descent in the diaspora.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals of African descent in the diaspora seeking to permanently return and reside in Ghana, or former Ghanaian citizens who lost their citizenship upon acquiring another nationality.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Right of Abode itself is a permanent residency status, granting indefinite stay in Ghana.
benefits: Indefinite residency in Ghana without the need to renew visas or residence permits.
Visa-free entry into Ghana at any time.
Permission to work, seek employment, or engage in business/profession without a separate work permit.
Exemption from many recurring permit fees required of other foreign residents.
Right to live permanently and own property in Ghana (with some limitations for non-citizens).
required_documents: Formal application letter addressed to the Minister for the Interior.
Completed prescribed Right of Abode form.
Two (2) current passport-size photographs.
Applicant's autobiography (for former Ghanaian citizens).
Copy of valid passport.
Medical report (specifically from the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) Clinic).
Valid non-citizen ID card (G-Card).
Police Clearance Certificate from country of origin and Ghana.
Two (2) attestation/character reference letters from Ghanaians of repute (Notaries Public, Lawyers, Senior public officers) with copies of their national IDs.
Evidence of financial means or independent livelihood (e.g., bank statements, employment letters, business documents).
Evidence of contribution to Ghanaian economic development (e.g., monetary value of shares, audited accounts, provision of employment to Ghanaians) (for persons of African descent).

Company's Documents (Companies Code, 3 years of audited accounts, SSNIT returns of Ghanaian employees, Tax Clearance Certificate (personal & company) for the past 6 years) (if applicable for business owners).
Proof of African descent (for persons of African descent).
Valid citizenship renunciation certificate (for former Ghanaian citizens).
Birth certificate (for former Ghanaian citizens).
Property records (indentures or site plans for any land or buildings owned in Ghana) (for former Ghanaian citizens).
application_process_steps: Establish lawful residency in Ghana (for persons of African descent, typically 2-5 or 7 years on a valid residence permit).
Gather all required documentation, ensuring foreign documents are legalized or apostilled if necessary.
Submit a formal application letter addressed to the Minister for the Interior through the Director of Immigration.
Undergo a verification process and due diligence/background checks by the Ghana Immigration Service.
Pay the relevant application fees.
Await final approval from the President of Ghana, following the Minister's recommendation.

visas.name: Self-Employment Permit (under Residence Permits)
visas.description: This permit is for foreign nationals who wish to reside in Ghana and engage in self-employed activities or establish their own business. It authorizes the holder to legally live and work in the country, contributing to its economy through their entrepreneurial endeavors.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign individuals who intend to establish and operate their own business or work for themselves in Ghana for an extended period.
visas.path_to_residency_description: A Permanent Residence Permit is generally available after holding temporary residence permits for a cumulative period of 5 to 7 years. Applicants typically need to demonstrate a real contribution to Ghana's economy, solid character, and a clean criminal record.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet eligibility criteria, maintain a compliant business/self-employment status, and have no criminal convictions. Renewal typically requires an updated application and submission of relevant documents.
benefits: Authorization to work legally in Ghana as a self-employed individual.
Grants the right to reside in Ghana for the permit's validity period.
Provides access to local healthcare and banking services.
Offers legal protection under Ghanaian immigration laws.
Ability to travel in and out of Ghana multiple times within the permit's validity without needing a new visa.
required_documents: Application letter addressed to the Comptroller-General of Immigration.
Valid passport (with at least six months' validity remaining and sufficient blank pages).
Completed Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) application forms.
Recent passport-sized photographs (taken not more than three months prior).
Certificate of Business Registration (including Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate to Commence Business, and Business Code, if applicable).
Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC) Registration Certificate (if applicable).
Company's current tax clearance certificate (if applicable).
Company's Audited Accounts of previous year (if applicable).
Medical Report from a Ghana Immigration Clinic in Accra (mandatory medical examination).
Police Report/Criminal Record Certificate from Home Country (apostilled and translated if necessary).
Curriculum Vitae/Resume of the applicant.
Professional and Educational Certificates (apostilled and translated into English if from a non-English speaking country).
Copy of Bio-data page of applicant's passport.
Copy of Non-Citizen Identification Card (if already obtained for previous stays exceeding 90 days).
Proof of financial means to support yourself while in Ghana (e.g., bank statements).
Letter of Support from Ministry, Department, or Agency (if required by the specific business sector).
application_process_steps: Ensure you hold a valid entry visa or are eligible for visa-free entry, and enter Ghana.
Gather all required supporting documents, ensuring foreign documents are authenticated and translated where necessary.
Undergo a mandatory medical examination at a Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) approved clinic.
Obtain a Non-Citizen ID Card if your stay will exceed 90 days.
Submit the complete application package, including the application letter, forms, and all supporting documents, to the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) headquarters in Accra or a regional office.

Pay the applicable government fees (Note: The exact fee for a standalone 'Self-Employment Permit' is not explicitly listed, but general Residence Permit fees apply, varying by nationality and other factors).

### Visas & Notes
- Residence permit available for investors and retirees
- Ghana Card required for long-term residents
- "Year of Return" diaspora program offers support for returnees

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Ghanaian citizenship by descent is a constitutional right for individuals born anywhere in the world who have at least one parent or grandparent who is or was a Ghanaian citizen. This pathway is designed to formalize ancestral ties and does not automatically confer citizenship, requiring a formal application to the Ministry of Interior. Required documents include proof of lineage (such as birth certificates or official records) and identification. Recent initiatives, such as the "Dual Citizenship Drive" for the Historic African Diaspora (launched in early 2026 but temporarily suspended for re-evaluation), have specified additional requirements like a two-year legal residence permit in Ghana and DNA proof to support Ghanaian descent.

Naturalization.desc: A foreign national may acquire Ghanaian citizenship by naturalization after meeting specific residency and character requirements. Applicants must have legally resided in Ghana for at least 5 years out of a 7-year period preceding the application, including continuous residence for at least 12 months immediately before applying. Key criteria also include being of good character (attested by two Ghanaian sponsors, such as notaries public, lawyers, or senior public officers), not having a criminal record, being able to speak and understand an indigenous Ghanaian language, demonstrating an intention to reside in Ghana, and providing proof of self-sufficiency. Additionally, applicants should show that they have made or are capable of making a substantial contribution to national progress or advancement, or can be easily assimilated into the Ghanaian way of life. The process involves application to the Minister and approval by the President.

Birthright.desc: Birth within the territory of Ghana does not automatically confer citizenship for those born after the 1992 Constitution. However, a person born in Ghana before March 6, 1957 (Independence Day), is a citizen if one of their parents or grandparents was also born in Ghana. A child found in Ghana who is under 7 years old and whose parents are unknown is presumed to be a citizen by birth. Children born anywhere to parents or at least one grandparent who is a Ghanaian national are considered citizens by birth through *jus sanguinis* (right of blood).

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreign national who is or was married to a Ghanaian citizen may apply to be registered as a citizen of Ghana. This pathway is generally more direct than naturalization. While the law does not explicitly impose a residency period, the immigration office may assess genuine integration and sometimes require proof of aggregate residence for about one year. The primary requirement is to demonstrate that the marriage is genuine and not solely for obtaining citizenship. Spouses retain their Ghanaian citizenship even if the marriage is later dissolved or the Ghanaian spouse dies, unless they formally renounce it. An adopted child under 16 years of age, whose adoptive parents are Ghanaian citizens, becomes a Ghanaian citizen by adoption.

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax:** Ghana operates a progressive personal income tax system. Rates range from 0% on the first GHS 5,880 annually (GHS 490/month) to a top rate of 35% on income exceeding GHS 20,000 per month.
*   **Tax Residency:** Residents are taxed on their worldwide income. An individual is generally considered a tax resident if they spend 183 days or more in Ghana in a year.
*   **Non-residents:** Non-residents pay a flat 25% on Ghanaian-sourced income.
*   **Corporate Tax:** The standard corporate tax rate is 25%. However, mining companies pay 35%, and petroleum companies pay 35-50%. Companies in free zones may enjoy a 10-year tax holiday.
*   **VAT:** Ghana's tiered VAT/levy system has an effective rate of approximately 21.9%, comprising a standard VAT of 15%, National Health Insurance Levy (NHIL) of 2.5%, and GETFund Levy of 2.5%. Small retailers may use a flat rate of 3%.
*   **Social Security:** Mandatory SSNIT (Social Security & National Insurance Trust) contributions are 5.5% for employees and 13% for employers (Tier 1 pension), plus a mandatory Tier 2 occupational pension (5% employee + 5% employer).
*   **Tax Treaty:** There is no tax treaty or totalization agreement between the U.S. and Ghana.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** A single expat in Accra needs roughly GHS 30,000 to 45,000 per month (about $2,750-$4,100 USD or €2,500-€3,800) for a comfortable lifestyle in a good neighborhood. A more modest lifestyle can be managed on GHS 15,000 to 25,000 monthly ($1,400-$2,300 USD or €1,300-€2,100). Housing is the largest expense, often 40-50% of the budget in prime Accra.
*   **Language:** English is the official language. Learning some basic phrases in local languages (e.g., Twi, Ga, Ewe) can enhance your experience and interactions.
*   **Safety:** Ghana is generally safe but exercise increased caution due to petty theft and opportunistic crime in busy areas. Avoid walking alone after dark and use trusted ride-hailing apps like Bolt. Secure neighborhoods for expats in Accra include Cantonments, Airport Residential Area, East Legon, Ridge, Roman Ridge, and Labone.
*   **Registration:** Foreigners staying over 90 days must apply for a residence permit through the Ghana Immigration Service. You will also need to register with the National Identification Authority (NIA) to obtain a Ghana Card, which is essential for banking and other services.
*   **Healthcare:** Public healthcare is improving but can be patchy; private hospitals in major cities offer higher standards. International health insurance is highly recommended.
*   **Infrastructure:** Be prepared for occasional power cuts (dumsor) and inquire about backup generator systems when securing accommodation. Internet connectivity has improved with options like Starlink.
